sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Kent County, Michigan?
sections.html:
Look for the County Administration Building at 300 Monroe Avenue NW, downtown Grand Rapids. Land contracts, liens and mortgages go through the same counter, under the Michigan Recording Act.

The office is careful about what it will not do. It does not supply blank deeds and it does not advise on how to prepare one. To change the names on a deed, the office lists three paths: a Michigan real property attorney, a title company, or a blank deed you complete yourself. It cautions that forms pulled from the internet may fall short of recording rules.

sections.h2: Why does the Kent County register of deeds see so many transfers?
sections.html:
Kent County is big. By the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate the county holds 675,232 people and 275,076 housing units across roughly 849 square miles of land. Records here start in 1836, the year the county was organized after being set off from Kalamazoo County in 1831.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 70.3%
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $289,900
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 2,398
  • People in the same house one year earlier: 87.9%

A county with that many owners and new construction has a steady flow of deeds, mortgages and discharges across one counter. For a seller, that means tidy paperwork before the closing.

sections.h2: What does recording cost at the Kent County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The base fee is $30 per document, and it has been in place since October 1, 2016. It covers deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and certified copies. The same fee schedule lists the add-ons you are most likely to meet when a house changes hands:

  • Assignments or discharges that cover several instruments add $3 per extra instrument, and the office asks you to limit these to 25 per document.
  • The treasurer's tax certification, needed for warranty deeds, land contracts and any deed with a covenant of warranty, is $5 per deed for up to 25 parcels and a quarter for each parcel after the 25th. That one goes on a separate check to the Kent County Treasurer.
  • Copies are $1 per page. Searches start at $5, and certifying a document adds $5.
  • Pay with cash, a check or a money order. The check is written to the Kent County Register of Deeds.

Electronic filers pay the statutory recording fee to the county, and any e-recording vendor can add its own processing fee on top.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies to a Kent County sale?
sections.html:
Add the two posted rates, $1.10 for the county and $7.50 for the state, and every $1,000 of price carries $8.60. Both come straight from Michigan's two transfer tax acts, MCL 207.504 and MCL 207.525.

Transfer tax on sample Kent County sale prices at the posted rates
Sale priceCounty taxState taxTotal
$150,000$165$1,125$1,290
$290,000$319$2,175$2,494
$400,000$440$3,000$3,440

The $290,000 row is near the Census median home value for Kent County, $289,900. The statute taxes each $500 or fraction of $500, so an odd price rounds the count up. There is no transfer tax on mortgages in Michigan.

sections.h2: Who owes the transfer tax, and how is an exemption claimed?
sections.html:
The seller, or grantor, owes it. Write the full price into the deed, or attach a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit. No fee applies to the affidavit so long as the deed mentions it.

Exemptions must be written on the deed itself. MCL 207.526 holds the state exemptions, such as a home passing from parent to child or grandchild, a deed from a mortgage foreclosure or given instead of one, a land contract before title passes, and a court-ordered transfer with no price set. A deed covering land in two counties has to split the price between them, and stamps are bought where the land lies.

sections.h2: Can you get any of the state transfer tax back?
sections.html:
Possibly, for a seller who held a principal residence exemption and sold at a price close to the property's earlier assessed value. MCL 207.526(u) exempts a conveyance of property that carried the principal residence exemption when the state equalized value is no higher than the value set at the first tax day after the home was built or acquired, and the sale was an arm's-length price.

Kent County's transfer tax page lists what a refund claim needs: the state refund application, copies of the recorded deeds showing the transfer tax stamp and proof of the sales price, and proof of the SEV from the local municipality. Copies of deeds come from the online deed search or from the office itself.

sections.h2: Can a deed be recorded electronically in Kent County?
sections.html:
Yes, through approved e-recording vendors, within a fixed window. Kent County accepts and processes electronic documents between 8 am and 5 pm Monday through Friday, excluding county holidays, and takes payment by ACH under its agreements with the vendors.

Kent reserves the right to reject any electronic filing that fails the Michigan Recording Act, and a party whose documents violate the state standards is cut off until further notice. Recorded documents return to the submitter in electronic form. An individual seller will usually leave this step to the closing office.

sections.h2: What should a Kent County seller do before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Settle the property tax first, because the register of deeds cannot take a warranty deed without a treasurer's certificate. MCL 211.135 asks for proof that no tax liens exist and that five years of tax are paid, so a delinquent balance gets cleared by closing. The Kent County Treasurer can quote that amount.

Also confirm the names on the deed match the owners of record. If a parcel's owner is unknown, the office suggests asking Equalization or the local assessor for the tax roll name, which may not match the true owner, and then searching recorded documents under it. After recording, the buyer has 45 days to give the local assessor the transfer notice under MCL 211.27a.

faqs.q: What does Kent County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The charge is $30 per document under the fee schedule effective October 1, 2016. Budget a further $5 for the treasurer's tax certification on a warranty deed, plus any vendor charge if a filer submits electronically.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax rate in Kent County?
faqs.a: It is $8.60 per $1,000 of price in total, split $1.10 county and $7.50 state. A $250,000 sale produces $2,150, owed by the seller unless the deed states an exemption.

faqs.q: Does the Kent County Register of Deeds help write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office does not supply blank deeds or offer advice on preparing them. It points people to a Michigan real property attorney, a title company, or a self-completed blank deed that meets recording rules.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Kent County without paying delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Not a warranty deed. State law requires a treasurer's certificate that taxes for the previous five years are paid. Quitclaim deeds with no warranty covenants are excepted.

faqs.q: How do I order a certified copy from Kent County?
faqs.a: Ask the Register of Deeds in person, by letter, or through its online document search. Copies cost $1 per page, certification is $5 per document, and a records search carries a $5 minimum.
